definitions.explanation: Indicates that something happens multiple times, more than what is typical. Somewhat more formal than よく.

examples.japanese: この{辺|あた}りでは{度々|たびたび}{地震|じしん}が{起|お}きる。
examples.english: Earthquakes occur frequently in this area.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{度々|たびたび}{遅刻|ちこく}するので、{上司|じょうし}に{注意|ちゅうい}された。
examples.english: He was repeatedly late, so his boss warned him.

notes:
USAGE:
Placed before the verb it modifies. Common in both spoken and written Japanese, though slightly more formal than よく or しょっちゅう.

{度々|たびたび}すみません is a very common apologetic phrase when bothering someone repeatedly.

WORD FORMATION:
{度|たび} (time, occasion) repeated → many times

SIMILAR WORDS:
- よく: often (neutral, most common)
- しばしば: frequently (more literary)
- しょっちゅう: all the time (informal, slightly negative)
- {何度|なんど}も: many times (emphasis on count)
